results.claim: Last-move compression: if H is k-uniform and its classical Maker-Breaker duration τ(H)=t is finite, then θ(H)≤max{k,t−1}. More precisely, θ(H)=k when t=k, while θ(H)≤t−1 when t>k.
results.proof_sketch: Every win requires k simultaneous Maker tokens, so t≥k and θ(H)≥k. Fix a classical strategy winning within t Maker moves. If t=k, Maker can execute it with k tokens. Suppose t>k. In the (t−1,*)-game, Maker follows this strategy and uses a fresh token on each of her first t−1 moves. Thus, until then, the position is exactly a possible classical-game position. An earlier win finishes the game. Otherwise, on move t the classical strategy prescribes an unoccupied vertex x that completes some edge e. Since Maker had not already won, x∈e and the other k−1 vertices of e are among her t−1 current tokens. Because t−1>k−1, at least one current token lies at a vertex u outside e. Maker legally moves that token from u to x. No vertex of e is vacated, so e becomes filled immediately. Hence t−1 tokens suffice.

results.claim: Uniform strict half-bound: every finite-theta k-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices satisfies θ(H)≤max{k,⌊(n−1)/2⌋}. In particular, if n≥2k+1 then θ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉−1.
results.proof_sketch: The already-proved classical duration bound gives τ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉. Applying last-move compression yields θ(H)≤max{k,τ(H)−1}≤max{k,⌈n/2⌉−1}=max{k,⌊(n−1)/2⌋}. When n≥2k+1, one has ⌈n/2⌉>k, so the maximum is exactly ⌈n/2⌉−1, strictly below the former half-vertex bound.

results.claim: Exact order obstruction: a finite k-uniform hypergraph can attain θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉ only when n∈{2k−1,2k}; both orders are attainable.
results.proof_sketch: If θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉ and ⌈n/2⌉>k, the strict half-bound gives the contradiction θ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉−1. Since filling a k-edge requires at least k tokens, equality also forces ⌈n/2⌉≥k. Consequently ⌈n/2⌉=k, equivalently n∈{2k−1,2k}. Conversely, on either order let H contain every k-subset as an edge. Fewer than k tokens cannot fill an edge. With k tokens, Maker places a new token on each of her first k turns. Before her kth turn at most 2k−2 vertices have been occupied, so a free vertex remains; after taking it, her k vertices form an edge. Thus θ(H)=k=⌈n/2⌉.

final_writeup:
No fixed k≥4 admits arbitrarily large examples attaining the half-vertex bound. Indeed, the stronger uniform estimate

θ(H) ≤ max{k, ⌊(n−1)/2⌋}

holds for every k-uniform H on n vertices with finite token number. Therefore, for every n≥2k+1,

θ(H) ≤ ⌈n/2⌉−1.

The key observation is that the final move of a bounded classical winning strategy does not require a new token. Let t=τ(H). If t>k, Maker follows a t-move classical winning strategy using fresh tokens for the first t−1 moves. On any branch that lasts until move t, the prescribed final vertex x completes a k-edge e. Exactly k−1 vertices of e were previously held, whereas Maker currently has t−1>k−1 tokens. She can therefore move a token situated outside e to x, retaining all of e and winning with only t−1 tokens. If t=k, exactly k tokens suffice. Thus θ(H)≤max{k,τ(H)−1}; combining this with τ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉ proves the displayed bound.

This also completely locates possible equality: θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉ can occur only for n=2k−1 or n=2k. It does occur at both orders for the complete k-uniform hypergraph. Hence equality is confined to two bounded orders for each fixed k and cannot occur on arbitrarily large hypergraphs.

Checked the compression argument branch-by-branch: early wins use at most t−1 fresh tokens, while a length-t branch has t−k≥1 eligible source tokens outside its terminal k-edge.
Checked the parity identity ⌈n/2⌉−1=⌊(n−1)/2⌋ and the threshold ⌈n/2⌉>k exactly when n≥2k+1.
Checked both boundary orders directly: complete k-uniform hypergraphs on 2k−1 and 2k vertices have token number exactly k.
